title: Beyond Temporal Proximity: Explanatory World Models for Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.13504v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Generative Recommenders increasingly use Reinforcement Learning (RL) to optimize outcomes that may appear hundreds or thousands of interactions after a decision. Standard RL propagates reward according to temporal proximity rather than explicit relevance, attenuating the signal assigned to distant but important actions and creating a source of sample inefficiency. We introduce Explanatory World Models (EWM), an attribution framework that uses explanations to identify the earlier events that plausibly contributed to a realized outcome. We instantiate EWM with a frontier language model and use its explanations as learning signals using a conservative hierarchical operator that recursively redistributes reward while preserving the undiscounted episode return. translated_title: 超越时间邻近性：面向强化学习中信用分配的解释性世界模型
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.13504v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：生成式推荐系统越来越多地采用强化学习（RL）来优化那些可能在决策发生数百甚至数千次交互之后才显现的结果。标准的强化学习依据时间邻近性而非显式相关性来传播奖励信号，这削弱了分配给那些距离遥远但至关重要的动作的信号，并成为样本效率低下的一个根源。我们提出了解释性世界模型，这是一个归因框架，利用解释来识别可能对最终已实现结果有贡献的早期事件。我们用一个前沿语言模型来实例化EWM，并通过一个保守的分层算子将其生成的解释用作学习信号，该算子在保持未折扣回合回报的前提下递归地重新分配奖励。为了探究什么样的解释才是有用的，我们受Halpern的实际因果理论、Lombrozo的解释简洁性理论以及De……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出解释性世界模型（EWM）框架，用语言模型生成的因果解释取代传统的时间邻近性来进行强化学习中的信用分配，通过保守分层算子递归重分配奖励并保持回合总回报不变，从而提升生成式推荐系统中长时程决策的样本效率。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Explanatory World Models (EWM), an attribution framework that replaces temporal proximity with language-model-generated causal explanations for credit assignment in reinforcement learning, recursively redistributing rewards through a conservative hierarchical operator while preserving undiscounted episode returns to improve sample efficiency in long-horizon decision-making for generative recommenders.
